events.notes: fiction:the party leaves the road or causeway

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], Hive-Touched Pack [T-01].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain needles the black water of Hollowmoot's dock-row, and lanterns gutter under sagging awnings as a Warden crier reads the morning tally: the Causeway holds, but Gullet Ford is 'watched.' A ferry-hand named Corrin fights to keep an overloaded skiff of refugees from swamping at the pilings, shouting for hands. Somewhere out past the reeds, faint and wrong, drifts a thin thread of song. The four of you are here — pulled by debt, duty, grief or hunger — when Corrin's eyes find you and she begs for help before the tide takes the last dry landing.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Easy now—let the current help us, not fight it. I've kept crews steadier than this through tighter spaces.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (I hurry down the dock toward Corrin, keeping my footing on the slick planks. I take position at the skiff's side and call out steady instructions—weight low, weight distributed—reading Corrin's panic and the refugees' fear. My voice is the one that's kept order on night-barges through worse weather. I steady the gunwale, guide a woman's foot to the safer position, nod to Corrin to hold the line.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I'm coming, Corrin! The rain's warning me—shift weight toward the stern or she'll swamp! These refugees won't die on my watch!

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous bolts across the rain-slicked dock, his eyes fixed on the struggling skiff and the dark water beneath it. He reads the patterns in the falling rain and the surge of the flood, calling urgent warnings to Corrin about the dangerous currents and weight distribution. His hands are already reaching to help steady the boat as he reaches the pilings.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Everyone off those heavy goods—NOW! Corrin, push to the shallow side. I've guided pilgrims through worse water than this, and we're not losing anyone today.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen strides down to the dock with absolute authority, boots splashing through the rain-slicked boards. She immediately takes command—pointing, calling out orders to dock-workers to lighten the skiff's load, organizing refugees with the voice of someone used to being obeyed. Her presence alone seems to cut through the panic.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I'm coming, Corrin! Hold the line!

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire runs across the slick dock toward the skiff, her watch-trained eyes quickly assessing the load distribution and the encroaching water. She moves to position herself at the boat's side, using her strength to help stabilize the hull and keep the refugees' weight centered against the rising tide.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: No—no, I've got it. I've *got* this. Corrin, hold steady—I won't let her slip!

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — overcome with Rapport: dice + - - + → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — overcome with Notice: dice 0 - - -, invoking Reads omens in the rainfall [AL-01] → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — overcome with Will: dice - + - + → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — overcome with Physique: dice 0 + 0 0, invoking Trained young in watch drills [MI-01] → Fantastic (+6) vs Great (+4): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text:
It comes together like a single held breath let go. Ysolde's voice cuts through the panic and the skiff steadies under her calm counting; Aldous reads the rain's slant and calls the exact moment to lean before a wave-surge would've rolled them; Morwen's bark has dock-hands hurling sacks of grain overboard without question, and Mire simply plants herself against the hull like a fifth piling, holding the line until the worst of the swell passes beneath them. Corrin hauls the last soaked child up onto the dock with a sob of relief, and the skiff — battered, half-swamped, but whole — scrapes safe onto the landing. For a moment there's only rain and gasping and the wet slap of rope on wood. Then, out past the reeds, the pale thread of that wrong song rises and fades again — closer than before — and everyone's eyes go to the drowned horizon, where a thin smear of smoke hangs over what should be Aldous's home village, silent as a held breath. Corrin follows his stare and goes quiet herself. "That's not cook-smoke," she says. "And Marrow's bells haven't rung in two days. I thought it was just the wet dampening the sound."

The refugees are ashore. The ford is drowned but the dock is dry, and for now, the stalking thing in the reeds keeps its distance.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The dock crier won't spare a boat for a dead village, so the four of you commandeer a narrow poling-skiff and push off the landing yourselves, leaving the lantern-light of Hollowmoot behind. The causeway's safety falls away fast; within a hundred yards you're threading standing dead trees and drowned rooftops, reed mats hiding who-knows-what beneath the black water, Aldous's old home a smudge of smoke on the grey horizon ahead. The swarm-song threads through the rain again, closer now, seeming to come from everywhere and nowhere in the reeds around you. Somewhere out past the tree-line, half-glimpsed, something with a hooked spear tracks your passage without yet closing the distance.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Water tells me everything. Thing's pinned in the shallows—we take the deep channel, it can't follow.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde plants her pole and reads the water with Reed-Kin eyes—the subtle disturbances, the silt-patterns of something stalking the shallows. She points toward the deeper channel ahead where the current runs faster and the creature's hunting ground falls away.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain shows me their hunger—and their terror. They fear bright fire, all of them. That's our edge.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous tilts his face to the rain, reading its delicate patterns as his eyes track the half-glimpsed shape moving through the reeds. The falling rain whispers its secrets to him—of feral hunger and a primal, bone-deep terror of flames. He grips the skiff's pole tighter, his jaw set with grim purpose.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I see you in the reeds. Come out where I can see you, hive-touched thing—or I'm coming out to find you.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen stands up in the skiff, deliberately defiant against the rain and the gathering dark. She plants her feet firm on the wet boards and turns toward the rustling in the reeds, her hand going to the wrappings of blessed ash at her belt. She's not waiting for it to close the distance. She's forcing the thing to answer—calling it out into the open like she's done with a hundred possessed souls before.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: There—thirty yards out, moving parallel with us. That's a scout, testing the line before the pack closes in. Everyone keep low and watch for the spear throw.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire plants herself in the center of the skiff, pole ready, her eyes locked on the half-glimpsed movement in the reeds. She reads the ripples in the black water, the way the rushes part and resettle, calculating the threat's depth and angle of approach. Her body goes rigid and poised—old watch drills still governing her bones—tracking where the attack will come from and where they have room to maneuver.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Notice: dice - - 0 +, invoking Speaks the forbidden hive-hymns [YS-04], Reads river currents like kin [YS-01] → Superb (+5) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 0 0 + → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Notice: dice + - + 0 → Great (+4) vs Terrible (-2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hive-Touched Scout attacks Morwen (physical): Mediocre (+0) vs Morwen's Athletics Abysmal (-3) — hit for 3

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The reeds answer all three readings at once. Ysolde's pole finds the deep channel's pull and she calls it out — that fast black water ahead is the way out of the scout's hunting ground. Aldous watches the thing flinch bone-deep from a flash of far-off lightning and grins fierce: whatever these things are, fire is a nerve laid raw. Mire doesn't just spot the scout — she reads its whole angle of attack before it moves, marking the exact line it'll need to close on the skiff. But Morwen's challenge lands too well. The shape in the reeds breaks cover with a snarl that isn't quite human anymore, and a hooked spear hisses low across the water, catching her hard in the shoulder as she stands exposed in the skiff. She rocks back against the gunwale, blood mixing with rainwater, but she's still standing, still glaring back into the reeds where the scout — alone, for now — waits to see what she does next.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Bleed then, you hive-scrawled thing. You hurt one of mine.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde plants her pole hard against the skiff's floor and uses the boat's rock to gain leverage. She reads the creature like she reads water—every shift in the reeds, every ripple of intention—and drives forward in a violent counterstrike. The pole becomes a weapon in her practiced hands, aimed at the exact spot where the scout will turn to follow through on its attack.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: You won't throw another spear while I'm drawing breath! The rain shows me your path, and I won't let it lead to her!

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous moves immediately to place himself between Morwen and the reeds, his pole raised as both staff and barrier. He reads the falling rain with desperate intensity, tracking the scout's likely angle of attack, and positions himself to intercept or counter with every ounce of strength he can muster.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: You marked me, creature? Perfect—now I'm going to show you what an exorcist's will looks like.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen pulls herself upright despite the wound, rainwater and blood streaming down her arm. She draws blessed ash from her belt and begins chanting—something old and deep, not prayers but a voice of absolute command. She exerts her full power as an exorcist, bending her Will directly against the scout's corrupted mind, forcing it to acknowledge her authority or break.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: There—now! Before it pulls back into the reeds!

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire pivots off the skiff's center post, using the moment of the scout's exposure to close hard. Her pole becomes a weapon as she cuts toward the open water where the creature stands, reading every ripple and shift in its stance. Watch-trained and certain, she commits to the strike while the thing is in the open and the group is ready.)

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: The thing dares? It dares wound her and think I'll hold back—I'll gut this creature in the open water where it bleeds like anything else!

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — attack with Stealth: dice - - 0 -, invoking Read the Stalker's Course [A-1.2.1], Reads river currents like kin [YS-01] → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS (Hive-Touched Scout stress 1)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — attack with Athletics: dice 0 0 - +, invoking Fear of bright flame revealed [A-1.2.2], Old militia discipline [AL-02], Marked by drowned ghosts [AL-01] → Legendary (+8) vs Fantastic (+6): SUCCESS (Hive-Touched Scout stress 2)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Will: dice 0 - 0 0, invoking Can calm a hive-touched victim [MO-03] → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — attack with Fight: dice 0 - + +, invoking Watching the Scout's Angle [A-1.2.3] → Epic (+7) vs Superb (+5): SUCCESS (Hive-Touched Scout mild consequence)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen's chant closes around the scout like a snare of iron before its body even understands it's caught — Bound by Exorcist's Command, and for one heartbeat the thing simply cannot flee. Ysolde's pole cracks into its ribs in the same instant Aldous drives forward from Morwen's side, both blows landing on a creature that has nowhere left to dodge, and it staggers, spear-arm going slack. Mire finishes it — her pole sweeping the scout's legs out from under it and driving it under the black water with a final, ugly crunch. It doesn't rise again; the reeds go still, the half-glimpsed shape gone, and for a moment even the wrongness of the swarm-song seems to falter and thin behind you. Rain hisses on empty water where a hunter was a moment ago. Ahead, past the drowned trees, the smoke over Marrow still climbs — thicker now that the scout's threat is behind you, and the bells that haven't rung in two days stay silent as your skiff noses on toward the smudge on the grey horizon.

costs.text: As Aldous plants his feet at the swamping pilings and stares into the churning black water to read its patterns, a jolt of memory from the Sunken Barge locks his knees — he freezes for one dangerous heartbeat, the skiff lurching unattended in his hands before he can force himself to move again.

Ysolde's counterstrike is pure fury, not tactics — she lunges past the skiff's balance point to land the blow, and for a moment she's the one exposed at the gunwale, pole overcommitted, if anything else is watching from the reeds.

violations.issue: The compel's complication (Aldous freezing over the 'Sunken Barge' memory, event 11) was fully narrated before the triggered Story Pile card (PS-13) was even drawn (events 12-13), so the drawn card's content could not have been used to build that complication as §6A requires ('The complication must involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread').

Scene-end tension adjustment credited '+1 fled/bypassed' toward a card the party actively confronted and overcame via four successful rolls, not fled, bypassed, or ignored — the stated justification does not match the logged fiction for that row of the §6 table.

Story Pile draw of PS-09 (triggered by Ysolde's accepted non-deck compel) has no logged follow-through: the rule requires 'the complication must involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread' and that 'the GM gains 1 free invoke on it,' but no subsequent event shows PS-09's tags used in the complication, the GM's free invoke being spent, or the thread/NPC being advanced. The requirement appears unmet in the visible log.

ambiguities.detail: Arm definition lists Attention; not modelled.

ambiguities.interim_ruling: Yes, GLOBAL cards placed on the rail give the GM 1 free invoke that scene.
All applicable rows are summed, then clamped to 1-6.

ambiguities.interim_ruling: Both: the aspect keeps 2 free invokes and the player may also peek.

ambiguities.interim_ruling: Both: the aspect keeps 2 free invokes and the player may also peek.

ambiguities.issue: When a player accepts a compel that did not come from a deck draw, §6A requires 'the complication must involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread.' In this log the compel's full complication was narrated at event 11 (Aldous freezing over the 'Sunken Barge' memory) *before* the triggered Story Pile draw (PS-13) happened at events 12-13. The spec does not say whether the pile card must be drawn first to seed the complication, or may be drawn afterward as a separate addition to the rail/fiction.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table ruled that the compel's immediate complication can be freely narrated by the GM, and the subsequently-drawn Story Pile card (PS-13) is treated as a follow-on rail addition to be woven into later scenes rather than a card whose content had to inform this specific compel.

ambiguities.issue: The Tension adjustment table only lists 'fled, bypassed or ignored a face-up THREAT or FACTION' (+1) and 'resolved a THREAT or filled a goal' (-1); it never mentions HAZARD cards. H-03 (used as opposition in this scene) appears to be a HAZARD, yet the scene-end tension note applied both rows to it.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated HAZARD as equivalent to THREAT/FACTION for the purposes of the §6 tension-adjustment table, since the rules are silent on HAZARD's treatment there.

ambiguities.issue: §6A states the GM gains 1 free invoke on a story card drawn via an accepted non-deck compel, and the event-log format note says GM free-invoke grants are logged as their own rows ('GM +1 free invoke'). No such row appears for PS-13 after events 12-13.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated the free invoke as automatically granted but only logged it if and when actually spent; since it went unused this scene, no separate grant row was written.

ambiguities.issue: The Fate event that triggers a Story Pile draw ('a player accepts a compel that did not come from a deck draw') fired at event 40, but the compel's complication was already fully narrated and resolved in that same event, before the pile card (PS-09) was drawn at event 42. The rule requires 'the complication must involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread,' but the drawn card cannot retroactively shape a complication that was already fictioned and accepted. The spec does not say whether the draw must happen before the complication is narrated.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table let the already-narrated compel stand as-is, treated the story draw as adding PS-09 to the rail as a forward-looking situation aspect/GM free invoke for later use, and did not retroactively tie PS-09's tags to the event-40 complication.

cost_checks.note: draw_id is empty in the costs/compels list for this compel; it is a normal Fate compel on Aldous's own live weakness tag 'Panics near deep water' (card AL-01, already in his binder), not a Session Deck draw. Per §3/§4, deck-draw costs only apply to ties/major costs from Session Deck rolls, so no drawn card was required here — the compel correctly used a live tag directly rather than a drawn card.

This is an ordinary fiction-based compel (draw_id 'YS-03' just labels which of Ysolde's own cards carries the invoked weakness tag), not a Session-Deck draw under §3/§4. It correctly used the live weakness tag 'Rage before reason' from that card, so the compel is well-formed even though the §3 'cost must use the drawn card's tags' rule doesn't technically apply here.

Story Pile draw of PS-09 following the free compel. Per §6A the complication must involve the drawn NPC/thread and the GM must gain and presumably spend a free invoke on it, but no notes or subsequent event show PS-09's tags being used anywhere in the scene; the compel it was supposedly tied to (event 40) was already narrated before this draw occurred.

friction.text: The Story Pile draw (PS-13) for Aldous's non-deck compel was resolved only after the compel's complication was already fully narrated, making it impossible to confirm the drawn card's content actually shaped 'the complication' as §6A requires.

The scene-end Tension note ('fled/bypassed +1, resolved -1') doesn't match the fiction: the party actively engaged with and succeeded against the obstacle across four rolls rather than fleeing, bypassing, or ignoring it, and the target card (H-03) appears to be a HAZARD rather than the THREAT/FACTION types the §6 table names.

Event 17's notes ('GM invokes: cuts off escape routes [H-03]') read like an active GM invoke, but no fate point or logged free-invoke grant accompanies it and the math shows no bonus was actually added — the ambiguous phrasing makes it hard to audit whether §3's 'a tag used to raise the difficulty cannot also be invoked by the GM on that roll' was respected.

Sequencing gap between the compel's narration (event 40) and its triggered Story Pile draw (event 42) makes §6A's 'complication must involve the drawn card' requirement effectively unverifiable and, on this log, unmet.

Success-with-style on create_advantage rolls stacking both 2 free invokes AND a Session-Deck peek happened three times in one scene (events 30/31, 32/33, 45/46), each needing the same ad hoc AMB-27 ruling — §3's outcome table doesn't clearly address create_advantage rolls, causing repeated table-level improvisation.

No tie or major-cost result occurred despite five combat/advantage rolls this scene, so the scene never exercised the core 'GM must build the cost from the drawn card' mechanic (§3); all extra bonuses came from the GM paying fate points to invoke existing rail/NPC tags instead, leaving the deck-draw-cost pathway untested.
